content: 1. In cases of disputes, the values expressed in grams per kilogram (g/kg) should be used as the standard. Specific clauses or sub-clauses are only required if they are relevant to the product in question. For example, the isomer ratio of an active ingredient is specified only when the ingredient is defined by a particular isomer ratio. Similarly, synergists and impurities are only specified when necessary and relevant. 2. Analytical Methods: Analytical methods must be peer-validated at a minimum. If the method is unpublished, full details and peer-validation data must be provided. For example, the method for determining the size of holes in flexible fabrics involves counting the number of holes in a defined area, either directly on the fabric or using indirect methods like photography. Conditioning of the fabric before testing should follow ISO 139 standards (4 hours at 20°C and 65% relative humidity). 3. Testing of Long-Lasting Insecticidal Nets (LN): The mesh size of nets is determined by counting the number of holes per square centimeter. Testing involves selecting five replicate squares, calculating the average, and noting the lowest value. The fabric should not be stretched or distorted during testing. For seam strength, five replicate tests are conducted with the seam centered on the test head. Flammability tests should follow EN 1102 standards, and observations such as after-flame time, after-glow time, and damage dimensions should be recorded. 4. Matrix Release Formulations (MR): These formulations are primarily used for public health protection and may also have agricultural applications. They involve active ingredients incorporated into or coated onto a polymer. The specifications for MR formulations should be divided into separate specifications for each polymer preparation type and the finished product. 5. Sampling and Storage Stability: Samples must be stored to prevent material deterioration and contamination. Sampling instruments should be clean and dry. For storage stability tests, samples taken before and after the test should be analyzed concurrently to minimize analytical errors. Accelerated storage tests involve storing the entire product at specified conditions (e.g., 54°C for two weeks) to evaluate physical properties. 6. Long-Lasting Treated Storage Bags (LB): These bags are woven polymer fiber bags treated with pesticides, designed for post-harvest storage of commodities like grains and seeds. The pesticide is released in a sustained manner to protect stored commodities from pest infestation for at least two years. The bags should comply with food contact material regulations, such as migration limits for polyolefins and heavy metals. The physical properties of the bags, including tensile strength and UV resistance, should meet ISO 23560 standards. 7. Flammability and Food Safety: Flammability testing is not part of the specification but should be conducted by the manufacturer according to 16 CFR Part 1610. The results should be presented on the package. For food safety, the polymer material used in the bags must be virgin (non-recycled) and comply with international food contact material regulations. 8. Microbial Pesticides: Guidelines for microbial pesticides, including bacteria, fungi, viruses, and yeasts, are under revision. Until the new version is available, the existing guidelines remain valid. 9. General Notes on Testing and Specifications: Methods for determining active ingredient content, isomer ratios, and impurities must be peer-validated. Sampling schemes should account for within-product variation, and sufficient sample sizes must be used to conduct all required tests. For physical tests, materials near seams or edges should not be tested to avoid bias. 10. Product Appearance and Quality: Products should appear clean and free from visible defects, such as poorly made seams or uneven weaves. They should be suitable for their intended use, such as storage bags with long-lasting activity and optional UV resistance.
